facts.fact: The U.S. President's Malaria Initiative profile states that monthly HMIS data collection is paper-based at village, health facility and hospital levels, and that the paper records go to the district, where the district health information officer enters them into the Zimbabwe DHIS2; no date is given, so the document's published year is used.

PMI states that monthly HMIS collection at health facility level is on paper, keyed at the district; its routine table gives 1,776 health facilities reporting into the HMIS/DHIS2 in 2022 (1,758 in 2018) with 96% of expected monthly reports received (97.2% in 2018), which counts reports received and not facilities entering them.

PMI states that the HMIS collects routine aggregate health information from four levels of the health system: primary (over 1,700 health centres, clinics and rural hospitals), secondary (about 140 district-level hospitals), tertiary (eight provincial hospitals) and quaternary (six hospitals); all report on paper. The document's published year is used.

PMI describes DHIS2 as the Ministry of Health and Child Care's system: donors and partners have very limited access to it, the ministry circulates no routine monthly DHIS2 report, and the malaria programme shares its data with PMI at bilateral meetings. The document's published year is used.

PMI states that electronic health records designed for deployment at each health facility, from which patient-level data would be aggregated into DHIS2, had been piloted in a small number of select districts, with no count given, and that the country continued to rely mainly on the existing paper-based HMIS. The document's published year is used.

PMI gives full digitisation of the HMIS through facility electronic health records as the current strategic direction of the Ministry of Health and Child Care, and says it is unclear whether the very substantial resources needed for scale-up will be made available. The document's published year is used.

note: The profile's date is a proxy: routine data run to 2022 and the text treats the second quarter of 2023 as still to come. The clinics value 'none' rests on the statement that facility-level collection is paper-based, not on a count. The policy table lists a National Digital Health Strategy (2021-2025) as a draft and does not say it names either system, so no plan fact is taken. No funder of the HMIS itself is named, so no finance fact is taken; malaria programming is said to rely almost wholly on the Global Fund and PMI. Community health worker data is said to be integrated into the HMIS, with no separate community system named. The profile also says DHIS2 had not yet been updated for the eight-contact antenatal schedule.
